To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Australian hotel industry is moving towards a high-commitment HRM model.

(1) hotel workplaces in general have been associated with high levels and different combinations of numerical and temporal flexibilities; (2) the adoption of high-commitment HR practices has been associated with a greater degree of functional flexibility; (3) the adoption of HR practices associated with a high-commitment approach to employee management has been associated with the adoption of numerical and temporal flexible strategies that are different in nature from those adopted in workplaces that have not adopted a high-commitment HRM approach.
the hotel industry is characterized by a low take-up rate of HRM, a high level of numerical and temporal flexibilization and an increasing use of functionally flexible work arrangements.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the extent to which the hotel industry has moved from a lowcost, low-commitment model to a high commitment, high performance approach, and the implications this has for the management of human resources.
the extent to which the hotel industry has moved from being a 'low road' to a 'high road' industry.
the extent to which the hotel industry is embracing high commitment HR practices, and how these practices are linked to different forms of organisational flexibility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hotel industry in general is not yet a bastion of high commitment HRM but that there are some signs of change, particularly at the luxury end of the industry.
the Australian hotel industry is moving towards a more strategic and sophisticated approach to HRM.
the hotel industry is moving towards more systematic HRM practices but that this process is not uniform across the industry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hotel industry in general is moving towards more sophisticated HR management techniques, although the extent to which this is happening varies according to the size of the hotel.
the hotel industry is undergoing a transition from a traditional low-cost, low-commitment approach to a high-commitment approach, but that this is not a uniform process.

while the hotel industry continues to be characterised by high levels of numerical flexibility and a low take up of HRM practices, the industry has not been immune to the pressures for functional flexibility and HRM.

the hotel industry is becoming more differentiated in its employment and HR practices, and that the industry is no longer a homogeneous sector.
the hotel industry is in transition.
